summary: NCCE frames prompt/context optimization as recommendation: it builds a catalog of context strategies (cluster-wise MIPROv2 warm-up, then LLM-reflector evolution) and trains a neural collaborative-filtering router that picks a context per input instance. Evaluated with GPT-4o-mini on three NLP reasoning/QA datasets (HoVer, SCONE, HotpotQA) against global prompt optimizers (APE, OPRO, EvoPrompt, TextGrad, MIPROv2, GEPA, OpenEvolve, POLCA).

claims.claim: Instance-wise context routing beats global context optimizers.
claims.evidence: Table 1 test accuracy: NCCE avg 74.8 vs best baseline POLCA 71.5; SCONE 89.7 vs GEPA-Merge 86.2; HoVer 74.7 vs OpenEvolve 73.8; asterisks denote p<0.05 but test type and number of runs not described in the main text.

claims.claim: Theoretical PAC bound justifies instance-wise routing.
claims.evidence: Theorem 1 under a Cluster Lipschitz Preference assumption (§3.4, App. B); assumption is not empirically checked.
Not tested: Appendix E admits experiments use a single base LLM (GPT-4o-mini) and cross-model transfer is open.

patterns.note: Searched/evolved context catalog with a learned router; evidence only on NLP QA, not coding agents.
Routes inputs to contexts rather than models; conceptually adjacent to routing.

methodology.sample: HoVer 1,520 test / SCONE 1,200 test / HotpotQA 2,000 test, with 500 train and 500 dev each (App. F Table 3).
methodology.baselines: APE, OPRO, EvoPrompt, TextGrad, MIPROv2, GEPA, GEPA-Merge, OpenEvolve, POLCA — current and reasonably strong prompt optimizers.
methodology.models: GPT-4o-mini task model, GPT-4o reflector, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings; single task LLM.
methodology.variance: Significance markers (p<0.05) in Table 1; seeds/number of runs not clearly reported.
methodology.ablations: Component ablation (Table 2), cluster number, data density, co-evolution rounds.
methodology.contamination_controls: Random held-out test split; no control for public QA datasets in GPT-4o-mini pretraining.

standards.peer_review: None indicated (no arXiv comment); includes a NeurIPS checklist, suggesting submission.
standards.artifacts: Text states 'Our code is publicly available' but no URL was extractable from the text; checklist claims open code.

biases.detail: One task LLM (GPT-4o-mini), acknowledged in App. E.
Optimization costs ~16k–105k API calls per dataset (Table 4) but accuracy-per-cost vs baselines is not compared.
'paradigm shift' framing for per-instance prompt selection.
No software-engineering or agent task evaluated.

verdict_reason: off-topic: per-instance prompt/context optimization evaluated only on NLP QA and fact-verification datasets with one model; no coding, agent, or harness evaluation, so it does not inform a software-engineering harness decision.
applicability: Does not transfer directly. A Java ingestion/delivery team would need tens of thousands of labeled evaluations per task to train such a router, and nothing shows the gains carry to multi-step coding agents, multi-repo work, or spec-driven workflows. At most, it is a weak hint that one global AGENTS.md/system prompt may underperform per-task context selection (which progressive-disclosure skills already approximate).
